content:
If you're a heavy Apple Watch user and participated in this summer's testing, you may have noticed that some existing apps fail to launch on watchOS 27. Apple has identified the issue and is automatically updating apps on behalf of developers to ensure compatibility.

The relevant updates will be rolled out via the App Store, with the release notes stating: "This app has been updated by Apple to prepare for compatibility with watchOS 27, and no new features have been added."

Apple notified developers this week that the update process will be completed by August 31.

watchOS 27 (along with iOS 27 and other new operating systems) is expected to be officially released around mid-September, so the necessary updates have been pushed out early.

Apple stated that because the arm64 architecture portion of some watchOS apps had issues, this measure was necessary. They appear to be automatically reprocessing and re-packaging the apps to fix binary compatibility problems, allowing existing apps to continue functioning normally without developers having to take any action.
